es.summary: Alteración de la capacidad de las plaquetas para agregarse y formar coágulos, aumentando el riesgo de sangrado.
key_points: Puede deberse a trastornos cuantitativos (trombocitopenia) o cualitativos (función plaquetaria).
Los fármacos antiplquetarios inhiben la activación o agregación plaquetaria.
El recuento plaquetario <150 000/µL o pruebas de agregación anormales indican disfunción.
El manejo incluye retirar agentes inhibidores y, si es necesario, transfusión de plaquetas.

pathophysiology: Las plaquetas se activan por colágeno y ADP, formando agregados mediante GPIIb/IIIa.
En la disfunción, se bloquean receptores (P2Y12, GPIIb/IIIa) o se reduce la producción de plaquetas.
La falta de agregación impide la formación del tapón plaquetario y la coagulación secundaria.
risk_factors: Uso de inhibidores P2Y12 (clopidogrel, ticagrelor), aspirina, eptifibatide, cangrelor.
Enfermedades hepáticas, síndrome de Bernard‑Soulier, Glanzmann.
Quimioterapia, radiación, infecciones virales (p. ej. VIH, hepatitis C).
Deficiencias nutricionales de vitamina B12 o ácido fólico.
diagnostics: Pruebas de agregación plaquetaria (ADP, colágeno, ristocetina).
Hemoglobina y hematocrito para evaluar pérdida sanguínea.
treatment: Suspender o ajustar dosis de antiplateletas según riesgo quirúrgico.
Transfusión de concentrado de plaquetas si <20 000/µL o sangrado activo.
Uso de agentes hemostáticos locales (gelatina, fibrina).
Corrección de deficiencias nutricionales (B12, ácido fólico).
complications: Mayor morbilidad en cirugías y procedimientos invasivos.
nursing_care: Evaluar signos de sangrado cada 4 h y registrar recuento plaquetario.
Monitorear hemoglobina/hematocrito y signos vitales (PA, FC).
Mantener acceso venoso de calibre adecuado para transfusión.
Aplicar presión directa a sitios de sangrado y usar apósitos hemostáticos.
Coordinar con laboratorio la obtención de pruebas de agregación.
patient_teaching: Informar sobre signos de sangrado y cuándo buscar ayuda.
Enseñar a evitar traumatismos bucales y usar cepillo de cerdas suaves.
Explicar la importancia de reportar todos los medicamentos, incluidos AINES.
Recomendar dieta rica en vitamina B12 y ácido fólico.
Indicar la necesidad de controles de laboratorio periódicos.

outcomes: Control del sangrado: sin evidencia de hemorragia activa en 48 h.
Hemoglobina estable: variación <1 g/dL en 72 h.

interventions.rationale: Detectar sangrado temprano permite intervención oportuna.

interventions.rationale: Facilita decisiones de suspensión antes de procedimientos.

interventions.action: Aplicar presión directa y apósitos hemostáticos cuando haya sangrado.
interventions.rationale: Detiene la pérdida sanguínea localmente.

interventions.action: Coordinar transfusión de plaquetas si recuento <20 000/µL o sangrado activo.
interventions.rationale: Aumenta la capacidad hemostática del paciente.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de sangrado y cuándo buscar ayuda.
interventions.rationale: Promueve autocuidado y detección precoz.

Presión arterial mantenida dentro de rangos normales para la edad.

interventions.rationale: Corrige déficit de volumen y mantiene perfusión tisular.

en.summary: Alteration of the ability of platelets to aggregate and form clots, increasing the risk of bleeding.
key_points: May be due to quantitative disorders (thrombocytopenia) or qualitative disorders (platelet function).
Antiplatelet drugs inhibit platelet activation or aggregation.
A platelet count <150 000/µL or abnormal aggregation tests indicate dysfunction.
Management includes discontinuing inhibitors and, if necessary, platelet transfusion.

pathophysiology: Platelets are activated by collagen and ADP, forming aggregates via GPIIb/IIIa.
In dysfunction, receptors (P2Y12, GPIIb/IIIa) are blocked or platelet production is reduced.
Lack of aggregation prevents formation of the platelet plug and secondary coagulation.
risk_factors: Use of P2Y12 inhibitors (clopidogrel, ticagrelor), aspirin, eptifibatide, cangrelor.
Chemotherapy, radiation, viral infections (e.g., HIV, hepatitis C).
Nutritional deficiencies of vitamin B12 or folic acid.
diagnostics: Hemoglobin and hematocrit to assess blood loss.
treatment: Discontinue or adjust antiplatelet dose based on surgical risk.
Platelet concentrate transfusion if <20 000/µL or active bleeding.
complications: Increased morbidity in surgeries and invasive procedures.
nursing_care: Assess bleeding signs every 4 h and record platelet count.
Monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit and vital signs (BP, HR).
Maintain appropriately sized venous access for transfusion.
Apply direct pressure to bleeding sites and use hemostatic dressings.
Coordinate with laboratory for aggregation studies.
patient_teaching: Inform about bleeding signs and when to seek help.
Teach to avoid oral trauma and use soft-bristled toothbrushes.
Explain the importance of reporting all medications, including NSAIDs.
Recommend a diet rich in vitamin B12 and folic acid.
Advise on the need for periodic laboratory monitoring.

outcomes: Bleeding control: no evidence of active hemorrhage within 48 h.
Stable hemoglobin: variation <1 g/dL within 72 h.

interventions.action: Assess catheter insertion site and mucous membranes every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Early detection of bleeding allows timely intervention.

interventions.action: Maintain an updated list of platelet-inhibiting medications.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates decisions to discontinue before procedures.

interventions.action: Apply direct pressure and hemostatic dressings when bleeding occurs.
interventions.rationale: Stops local blood loss.

interventions.action: Coordinate platelet transfusion if count <20 000/µL or active bleeding.
interventions.rationale: Increases patient hemostatic capacity.

interventions.action: Educate the patient about bleeding signs and when to seek help.
interventions.rationale: Promotes self-care and early detection.

outcomes: Fluid balance: intake and output within ±500 mL/24 h.
Blood pressure maintained within normal age ranges.

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of volume deficit or excess.

interventions.action: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Changes may indicate hypovolemia or overload.

interventions.action: Administer IV fluids per prescription and assess clinical response.
interventions.rationale: Corrects volume deficit and maintains tissue perfusion.

interventions.action: Observe for edema or dehydration signs in skin and mucous membranes.
interventions.rationale: Identifies complications of fluid management.

interventions.action: Teach the patient the importance of reporting dizziness or intense thirst.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection of volume changes.

summary.0.quote: Individuals with thrombocytopenia may have increased risk for bleeding as their platelet count decreases, resulting in difficulty creating blood clots and controlling hemostasis.

key_points.1.quote: Mechanism of Action Inhibits platelet activation through binding to the P2Y12 class of ADP receptors on platelets

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: There are currently four P2Y12 inhibitors available in the United States: clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor, and cangrelor.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Moreover, alcoholic thrombocytopenia is compounded by nutritional deficiencies in folate , thiamine, and vitamin B 12 (Silczuk & Habrat, 2020).

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Some symptoms of bleeding are blood in the stool; dark, tarry-appearing stools; blood in the urine; epistaxis; gingival bleeding; very severe headache; coffee-ground emesis; and hemoptysis.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: These cues include bruising, purpura , petechiae , excessive bleeding from minor cuts or injuries, bleeding from gums, hematomas, hematuria, heavy menstrual bleeding, frequent or spontaneous nosebleeds, and blood blisters in the mouth or on the body.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Other symptoms include nose bleeds, bleeding gums, or prolonged bleeding times after minor invasive procedures (Silczuk & Habrat, 2020).

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Monitor the client for bleeding via decreases in hemoglobin and/or hematocrit and monitoring for other signs/symptoms; monitor platelets to identify bleeding risk.

sections.complications.0.quote: This can manifest in many different ways, including excessive bleeding in response to trauma or during surgery, gastrointestinal bleeding, or spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Monitor the client for bleeding via decreases in hemoglobin and/or hematocrit and monitoring for other signs/symptoms; monitor platelets to identify bleeding risk.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Actions to reduce further bleeding include avoiding sharp objects and using an electric razor or a soft toothbrush to avoid tissue integrity issues.

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: Nurses should monitor laboratory tests and vital signs, administer medication, take safety precautions, and educate the patient about their condition.
